To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the measured transverse hadron spectra in central heavy-ion collisions from SIS to RHIC energies are well reproduced within the UrQMD transport approach, which includes hadronic and partonic degrees of freedom, (ii) in the case of central Pb+Pb collisions at RHIC, the transverse spectra are reproduced by a pure hadron-string transport model, which excludes partonic degrees of freedoms.

(i) the measured K± and pion spectra in central Au+Au collisions at AGS energies are not well described by default transport models; (ii) the additional pressure, which is required to reproduce the measured K± spectra, can be explained in terms of strong interactions in the partonic phase of Au+Au collisions, and (iii) this pressure can be estimated in a model-independent manner from lattice QCD calculations.
the observed pressure in central heavy ion collisions at SPS energies is due to partonic interactions in the quark-gluon plasma phase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the properties of the strongly interacting matter created in relativistic nucleus-nucleus collisions.
the study of hadronic interactions and the properties of strongly interacting matter in the energy range from 1 GeV to several TeV.
the study of the properties of the strongly interacting quark–gluon plasma (sQGP) formed in relativistic heavy-ion collisions at the CERN SPS, RHIC and LHC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data on K± transverse spectra are consistent with the existence of a pressure in the early phase of heavy-ion collisions at SPS and RHIC energies.
the measured pressure is not yet understood in terms of a quantitative theoretical model calculation.

the data on the K± transverse spectra are not yet fully explained by the present microscopic transport models and that a more detailed study of the K± transversal spectra from central Au+Au and Pb+Pb collisions at the top SPS energies is needed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the transverse mass spectra of K± mesons in central Au+Au collisions at RHIC energies are consistent with the assumption that the pressure in the partonic system is about 1/4 of the pressure in a hadronic system at T ≈ 150 MeV.
the measured K± spectra are compatible with the assumption of strong partonic interactions in central Au+Au collisions at SPS energies.

the transverse pressure observed in the K± spectra is not a unique feature of heavy-ion collisions but can also be observed in proton-proton and proton-nucleus collisions at the LHC energies, and that this pressure is not a unique signal of the QGP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transverse pressure is an important ingredient of a realistic description of the space-time evolution of relativistic heavy-ion collisions.
we are seeing the same effect in the K± spectra at SPS and RHIC energies.
the observed pressure is not a unique feature of heavy ion collisions, but is also seen in p+p and p+A collisions at the LHC and RHIC energies.
